behavioral_notes.observation: On completion, sets state='done' + end_datetime, then for certification surveys that were passed (scoring_success) it sends certification_mail_template_id with the PDF and, if certification_give_badge, runs the gamification.challenge cron (_cron_update) to award certification_badge_id (gamification.badge). It also fires _notify_new_participation_subscribers (mail.thread post) and strips inactive conditional questions. None of these cross-model effects (mail + gamification + messaging) are visible in metadata.

Scoring is Python-computed, not metadata: per-line answer_score/answer_is_correct depends on question_type (choice -> suggested_answer.answer_score/is_correct; numerical/date/datetime -> exact match against question.answer_*). In live sessions with session_speed_rating, score is time-decayed (100% under 2s, then linear down to 50%). user_input.scoring_percentage = sum(line scores)/total_possible_score, and scoring_success = percentage >= survey.scoring_success_min; both stored compute_sudo for perf.

9 question_types (simple_choice, multiple_choice, text_box, char_box, numerical_box, scale, date, datetime, matrix) each have bespoke server-side validation: mandatory checks (constr_mandatory), email-format (validation_email), length/value/date ranges (validation_*), single-answer enforcement for simple_choice, and full-row coverage for matrix. char_box answers can be saved as the respondent email/nickname. Validation logic lives only in code.

Public /survey/* routes are guarded by a two-token scheme (survey access_token + per-attempt answer_token) resolved sudo in _fetch_from_access_token; _check_validity returns business codes (survey_closed, survey_auth, token_required, answer_deadline, answer_wrong_user, etc.). AJAX navigation (begin/next_question/submit) re-validates each call, enforces attempts_limit and time limits server-side to prevent cheating, and conditional 'trigger' questions drive which question is served next via _get_next_page_or_question.

A survey can run as a synchronous live quiz: action_start_session sets session_state and a numeric session_code (4-10 digits, unique), attendees join via /s/<code>; the host advances questions (session_question_id) broadcasting over bus.bus; next question for conditional surveys is chosen from _get_session_most_voted_answers (collective audience answers); a leaderboard (_prepare_leaderboard_values) ranks attendees by scoring_total. Entirely behavioral, not in metadata.

30 JS files, 9 XML templates, 2 OWL components (SurveyQuestionTriggerWidget, SurveySurveyActionHelper) plus ~14 public.interactions widgets (SurveyForm, SurveyTimer, SurveyImageZoomer, SurveyResult, survey_session_chart/leaderboard/manage, survey_print, survey_quick_access). Asset bundles include dedicated survey.survey_assets (15) and survey.survey_user_input_session_assets (6).

classification.rationale: Survey is a horizontal assessment/feedback engine, not a primary value-creating line. It transforms nothing (not chain), runs no case-by-case solution loop as its core (not shop), and provides no matching/mediation infrastructure (not network) - it is a reusable support capability consumed by primary activities: recruitment screening, eLearning course quizzes/certifications (slides), marketing/NPS feedback, and the rating module. The record rules confirm this cross-cutting role by partitioning survey.user_input on survey_type so specialized embedders own their own data. Best PCF fit is 13.0 Develop and Manage Business Capabilities (capability/competency measurement, knowledge & certification via gamification badges); secondary fits are 3.5.x customer/market feedback (manifest category Marketing/Surveys) and 7.x human-capital competency assessment when used by HR/eLearning.
